Classical Ray Tracing Integration is a volume rendering technique that computes pixel color by combining background transmission (attenuated by absorption) and uniform in-scattering [S2, S5].

The claim describes 'Classical Ray Tracing Integration' as a technique that computes pixel color by combining background transmission and uniform in-scattering. However, Source [S2] describes a specific, simplified method for a spherical object (often referred to as the 'first 3D image' or basic volume rendering) that uses this formula. Source [S5] describes the actual 'Classical Ray Tracing Integration' (introduced by Kajiya and Von Herzen) as a technique that traces rays through participating media in small segments, integrating illumination and attenuation along the path, rather than using a simple closed-form combination of background transmission and uniform in-scattering. The claim incorrectly attributes the specific spherical approximation from [S2] to the general 'Classical Ray Tracing Integration' technique described in [S5]. Furthermore, [S5] explicitly states that the classical method involves segment-by-segment integration and accounting for material properties, which contradicts the 'uniform in-scattering' and simple combination formula presented in the claim.
